messages:
maya: Quick alert — during the canary for the kernel-selection optimizer (auto-route -> kernel-v2) we saw a transient OOM spike across a small subset of requests. Reproduced on two pods, ~6/120s tail. attaching profiler snippet below.

deploy-bot: deploy kernel-v2 to canary group (canary-4) at sha=6c7b2f

maya: profiler excerpt: ```
GPU memory high watermark: 12.1GB  (limit 12.0GB)
Active allocations: 240MB per workspace
KV cache occupancy: 78% (hot keys: /user/chat/*)
Batching distribution: 70% small (<=64 tokens), 30% large (>256)
Recent change: kernel-v2 selects larger temporary workspaces for conv attention path
```

ian: thanks, looking. initial thought: kernel-v2 increases workspace_size for >128 tokens to avoid recompute, but for mixed batching it can push working set over device limit.

sunita: can we toggle workspace_size heuristics at runtime? if yes, we should decouple long-seq fast-path from default for canary.

eli: workaround options: 1) rollback kernel-v2 selection rule 2) enable request-shaping CB to reject requests >256 tokens to canary 3) force smaller workspace_size (e.g., 0.75x) for canary pods 4) shrink kvcache TTL for this canary to free GPU pinned memory.

maya: i'm for option 3 + 2 short-term. avoid full rollback unless we hit more than 1% errors/5m. send config patch?

ian: pushed quick toggle to canary config: ```
canary.kernel_v2.workspace_scale=0.75
canary.circuitbreaker.max_concurrent_tokens=35000
canary.request_shape.reject_above_tokens=256
```

ops-bot: config apply succeeded on canary-4 (3 pods).

sunita: initial telemetry post-tweak: memory headroom regained ~700MB, OOMs stop within 90s. but tail latency for >200 tokens rose slightly (p95 +40ms).

eli: that's expected: smaller workspace -> more micro-recompute for long sequences. cost vs latency tradeoff. We should record for Optimize to tune batching heuristics for mixed workloads.

maya: agreed. next actions: 1) add temporary circuit breaker (reject/queue >256 tokens) for canary 2) keep workspace_scale=0.75 until we validate kernel-v2 memory accounting changes 3) reduce kvcache TTL from 60m -> 5m for canary to free pinned KV pages 4) create rollback playbook if OOMs resume.

ian: i've created a short runbook note and a rollback command snippet: ```
# rollback kernel selection rule
redwoodctl routes update --route canary-4 --kernel-selection kernel-v1
```

maya: labeling this thread as "postmortem-wip" — can someone add perf profile + flamegraph capture for the two offending traces? need to see where extra allocs happen (kv copy vs workspace alloc).

eli: grabbing flamegraphs now, will upload to S3 and link.

sunita: also adding a test in perf-suite: mixed-batch-seq-distribution to run overnight with workspace_scale variations and kvcache pressure simulation.

ops-bot: incident counter updated: OOM-1887654321 created. severity: S2. assigned to eng-runtime oncall.

maya: Thanks team. If OOMs resume after config revert we'll do a hard rollback to kernel-v1 and open a retro. For now the canary is stable. I'll update the playbook with the exact commands and thresholds we used. :thumbsup:

ian: note for follow-up: evaluate adaptive workspace sizing that considers current kvcache pinned pages + per-batch max_seq. Could avoid oscillation between recompute and OOM.

eli: +1. also add telemetry: emit workspace_bytes_requested and kvcache_pinned_bytes per-request to help Optimize recommendations.

maya: created a short checklist in the runbook: [1] toggle workspace_scale to 0.75, [2] enable reject_above_tokens CB, [3] reduce kvcache TTL to 5m, [4] capture flamegraphs, [5] monitor OOM rate for 30m -> rollback if >1% errors. copying here for audit.

sunita: copying to #eng-runtime-runbooks repo after lunch.

maya: closing thread for now, will post links to perf artifacts once uploaded.
